{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the sales data
sales_df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert revenue to float, coercing errors to NaN
sales_df['revenue'] = pd.to_numeric(sales_df['revenue'], errors='coerce')

# Identify rows where revenue is NaN (invalid)
invalid_revenue_mask = sales_df['revenue'].isnull()

# Check if any of these invalid revenue rows have status 'completed'
invalid_completed = sales_df[invalid_revenue_mask & (sales_df['status'] == 'completed')]
invalid_completed_count = len(invalid_completed)

# Also check if any 'completed' orders have zero revenue
completed_zero_revenue = sales_df[(sales_df['status'] == 'completed') & (sales_df['revenue'] == 0)]
completed_zero_revenue_count = len(completed_zero_revenue)

# Total completed orders (excluding invalid revenue and zero revenue)
# We assume that a valid completed order must have a non-zero revenue
valid_completed_orders = sales_df[(sales_df['status'] == 'completed') & (sales_df['revenue'].notnull()) & (sales_df['revenue'] > 0)]
valid_completed_count = len(valid_completed_orders)

# Summary
invalid_completed_count, completed_zero_revenue_count, valid_completed_count"}
